examples.ko: 그는 본디 조용한 사람이라 말이 별로 없어요.
examples.en: He is quiet by nature, so he doesn't talk much.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 본디 학교로 쓰던 곳이에요.
examples.en: This building was originally used as a school.

examples.ko: 본디 계획은 오늘 떠나는 거였는데 비 때문에 미뤘어요.
examples.en: The original plan was to leave today, but we postponed because of rain.

examples.ko: 사람은 본디 착하게 태어난다고 생각해요?
examples.en: Do you think people are born good by nature?

examples.ko: 이 노래는 본디 다른 가수가 불렀어요.
examples.en: This song was originally sung by a different singer.

examples.ko: 본디 성격이 급한 편이라 기다리는 게 힘들어요.
examples.en: I am impatient by nature, so waiting is hard for me.

explain: '원래'와 뜻이 같지만 조금 예스럽고 글말 느낌이 나요. 일상 대화에서는 '원래'를 훨씬 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: He is a quiet person by nature.
phrases.nuance_ko: '본디'와 뜻이 같지만 말할 때 훨씬 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 본디 but much more common in everyday speech.

phrases.en: This road was originally a narrow country road.
phrases.nuance_en: Less old-fashioned than 본디 but more written in tone than 원래.

phrases.example: 고장 난 의자를 원래대로 고쳐 놓았어요.
phrases.en: I fixed the broken chair back to how it was.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음 상태 그대로 되돌린다고 할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is put back exactly as it was at first.

explain_en: It means the same as '원래' but sounds a bit archaic and bookish. In daily conversation people say '원래' much more.

examples.ko: 담당자가 사고 경위를 소상히 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: The person in charge explained in detail how the accident happened.

examples.ko: 그 일은 제가 소상하게 알고 있어요.
examples.en: I know that matter in full detail.

examples.ko: 설명이 소상해서 이해하기 쉬웠어요.
examples.en: The explanation was thorough, so it was easy to understand.

examples.ko: 소상한 안내문 덕분에 어렵지 않게 신청했어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the detailed notice, I applied without difficulty.

examples.ko: 설명서가 소상하지 않아서 몇 번이나 물어봤어요.
examples.en: The manual wasn't detailed enough, so I had to ask several times.

examples.ko: 이 책은 설명이 소상하니까 처음 하는 사람도 따라 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: This book's explanations are thorough, so even a beginner can follow along.

explain: '자세하다'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 빠짐없이 꼼꼼하다는 느낌이고, '소상히 설명하다', '소상히 밝히다', '소상히 알다'처럼 말하거나 아는 내용에 주로 써요. '소상공인'의 '소상'과는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.example: 선생님의 소상한 설명 덕분에 쉽게 이해했어요.
phrases.en: Thanks to the teacher's detailed explanation, I understood it easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ/은'을 붙여 빠짐없이 꼼꼼한 설명을 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describes an explanation that is thorough, leaving nothing out.

phrases.en: The company explained the cause of the accident in detail.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소상히'로 바꿔 숨김없이 자세히 알린다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the adverb form 소상히, it means making something known in full detail.

phrases.example: 아직 계획이 소상하지 않아서 더 알아봐야 해요.
phrases.en: The plan isn't detailed yet, so I need to find out more.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내용이 충분히 자세하지 않을 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form is used when the content isn't detailed enough.

explain_en: It is close to '자세하다' but feels thorough, leaving nothing out, and is mostly used with explaining or knowing, as in '소상히 설명하다', '소상히 밝히다' and '소상히 알다'. The '소상' in '소상공인' (small business owner) is a different word.

examples.ko: 사극에서 주인공은 억울하게 역적으로 몰렸어요.
examples.en: In the historical drama, the hero was unjustly branded a traitor.

examples.ko: 그는 왕을 배신한 역적이라고 불렸어요.
examples.en: He was called a traitor who betrayed the king.

examples.ko: 역적의 가족까지 벌을 받던 시대였어요.
examples.en: It was an era when even a traitor's family was punished.

examples.ko: 역적이 되고 싶은 사람은 아무도 없어요.
examples.en: Nobody wants to become a traitor.

examples.ko: 이 드라마는 역적을 다룬 이야기예요.
examples.en: This drama is a story about a traitor.

examples.ko: 친구가 약속을 어겼다고 저를 역적 취급해요.
examples.en: My friend treats me like a traitor because I broke a promise.

explain: 옛날에 나라나 왕을 배신한 사람을 가리켜서 사극에서 많이 들어요. '반역자'보다 사극 느낌이 강하고, 요즘은 약속을 어긴 친구에게 농담으로 '이 역적아' 하고 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: A loyal subject was branded a traitor overnight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 억울하게 역적이라는 누명을 쓸 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set phrase for being falsely accused of treason.

phrases.nuance_ko: '역적'보다 사극 느낌이 덜하고 더 일반적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less of a historical-drama feel than 역적, and more general.

phrases.en: You broke your promise, you traitor!
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 친구끼리 농담으로 쓰는 반말 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A joking casual-speech expression between close friends.

explain_en: It refers to someone who betrayed the country or the king in the old days, and you hear it a lot in historical dramas. It feels more like period-drama speech than '반역자', and today people sometimes joke '이 역적아' to a friend who broke a promise.

examples.ko: 오빠가 이등병으로 입대했어요.
examples.en: My older brother enlisted as a private second class.

examples.ko: 이등병은 군대에서 가장 낮은 계급이에요.
examples.en: A private second class is the lowest rank in the army.

examples.ko: 아들이 이등병 때 쓴 편지를 아직 가지고 있어요.
examples.en: I still keep the letter my son wrote when he was a private.

examples.ko: 이등병이 선배들에게 인사를 했어요.
examples.en: The private greeted the senior soldiers.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 이등병부터 하사까지 올라갔어요.
examples.en: My uncle rose from private second class to sergeant.

examples.ko: 영화에서 이등병이 처음으로 총을 쏴요.
examples.en: In the movie, a private fires a gun for the first time.

explain: 한국군에서 가장 낮은 병사 계급이에요. 이등병 다음이 '일병', '상병', '병장'이에요. 군 이야기를 나눌 때 '이등병 때', '이등병 시절'이라고 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: My private second class days were the hardest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군 생활을 돌아볼 때 시기를 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to a period when looking back on military life.
phrases.en_equiv: when I was a private second class

phrases.en: My younger brother enters the army as a private second class next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입대하면 가장 낮은 계급인 이등병부터 시작한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means one starts at the lowest rank, private second class, upon enlisting.
phrases.en_equiv: to enlist as a private second class

phrases.example: 석 달 뒤에 이등병에서 일병이 돼요.
phrases.en: In three months he is promoted from private second class to private first class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계급이 올라가는 순서를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe moving up in rank.
phrases.en_equiv: to be promoted from private second class to private first class

explain_en: The lowest enlisted rank in the Korean military. After 이등병 come 일병, 상병 and 병장. When people talk about their service, they often say 이등병 때 or 이등병 시절.

en: to be in hiding; to lie low

examples.ko: 형사들이 범인이 올 만한 곳에서 잠복하고 있어요.
examples.en: Detectives are staking out the place where the criminal might come.

examples.ko: 감기 바이러스가 몸속에 잠복해 있다가 피곤하면 나타나요.
examples.en: The virus lies dormant in your body and shows up when you're tired.

examples.ko: 고양이가 풀숲에 잠복해서 새를 노려요.
examples.en: The cat lies in wait in the grass and eyes the bird.

examples.ko: 그는 몇 달 동안 조용히 잠복하며 때를 기다렸어요.
examples.en: He lay low quietly for months, waiting for his time.

examples.ko: 기자가 현장에 잠복했다가 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: The reporter waited in hiding at the scene and then took the photo.

examples.ko: 병이 잠복하는 기간은 보통 얼마나 돼요?
examples.en: How long is the incubation period of the disease usually?

explain: 그냥 '숨다'와 달리 때를 기다리며 몰래 숨어 있다는 느낌이 있어요. 수사에서는 '잠복 수사', 병에서는 '잠복기'라는 짝말로 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 '숨어 있다'라고 말해요.

phrases.example: 경찰이 어제부터 잠복 수사를 하고 있어요.
phrases.en: The police have been conducting a stakeout investigation since yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 범인을 잡으려고 숨어서 지켜보는 수사를 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set phrase for an investigation where police hide and watch for a suspect.

phrases.en: This illness has an incubation period of about a week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병에 걸린 뒤 증상이 나타나기 전까지의 기간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the period after infection before symptoms appear.

phrases.en: The criminal was lying in wait near the building.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잠복하다'의 상태를 나타내는 말로, 숨어서 계속 기다리고 있다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the ongoing state of staying hidden and waiting.

explain_en: Unlike plain '숨다', it implies hiding quietly while waiting for the right moment. It pairs with '잠복 수사' (stakeout) and '잠복기' (incubation period). In daily speech people say '숨어 있다'.

examples.ko: 급하게 돈이 필요해서 시계를 전당포에 맡겼어요.
examples.en: I needed money urgently, so I left my watch at a pawn shop.

examples.ko: 영화에서 전당포 주인이 반지를 살펴보는 장면을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a scene in a movie where a pawnbroker examines a ring.

examples.ko: 우리 동네에는 전당포가 하나도 없어요.
examples.en: There isn't a single pawn shop in my neighborhood.

examples.ko: 전당포에 맡긴 물건을 찾으러 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to retrieve the item I had left at the pawn shop.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 전당포 앞에서 한참 망설였어요.
examples.en: My uncle hesitated for a long time in front of the pawn shop.

examples.ko: 전당포를 하시는 할아버지가 금반지 값을 알려 주셨어요.
examples.en: The grandfather who runs a pawn shop told me the price of the gold ring.

explain: '전당포에 맡기다'와 '전당포에서 찾다'를 짝으로 외워 두면 편해요. 영화나 드라마 장면에 나오는 곳이라 이야기 속에서 자주 만나요.

phrases.en: I left my ring at a pawnshop and borrowed money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 맡기고 돈을 빌릴 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing for leaving an item to borrow money.

phrases.en: The pawnshop owner slowly examined the watch.
phrases.nuance_en: A character who often appears in films and stories.

phrases.en: I paid back the money and got my watch back from the pawnshop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맡긴 물건을 돈을 내고 되찾을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you pay and get back an item you left.
phrases.en_equiv: to get back from a pawnshop

explain_en: It helps to memorize '전당포에 맡기다' (leave at a pawn shop) and '전당포에서 찾다' (retrieve from one) as a pair. It is a place that shows up in movie and drama scenes, so you often meet it in stories.
